name: Lingual braces
summary: Braces bonded behind the teeth to hide them; discreet, but linked to more tongue and speech trouble than outer braces.
lead: Lingual braces are fixed orthodontic appliances bonded to the tongue-facing (inner) surfaces of the teeth rather than the outer surfaces, so that they are largely hidden from view.
claims: Braces, especially with extractions or rubber bands, can recess the face or narrow it
Braces improve how a person looks

name: Miswak / chew stick
summary: A traditional twig toothbrush from the arak tree; small trials link it to less plaque, but whitening claims are untested.
lead: Miswak is a traditional tooth-cleaning stick made from the twigs, stems or roots of the Salvadora persica tree, also called the arak or peelu tree. One end is chewed or peeled to expose fibres that act as bristles. Neem twigs (Azadirachta indica) serve a similar purpose in parts of South Asia, where they are known as datun.

name: Colored / circle contact lenses
summary: Tinted or enlarging contact lenses that change eye colour; FDA treats them as prescription medical devices with infection risks.
lead: Colored contact lenses, also called cosmetic, decorative or fashion lenses, change the apparent colour of the eye. Circle lenses, also called big-eye lenses, are a type of cosmetic lens that adds a coloured or dark ring to enlarge the apparent size of the iris.
claims: Lighter eye colour from lenses gives a noticeable increase in looks
Lenses can be bought online without an eye exam or measurements
Coloured lenses are a 'cope' that does not help

name: Foot orthotic insoles
summary: Shoe inserts sold for comfort, gait and height; evidence is for heel pain, with none found for looks or posture.
lead: Foot orthotic insoles, also called shoe inserts, foot orthoses or orthotics, are removable supports placed inside footwear. They are sold for comfort, arch support, pain relief, orthopaedic correction, athletic performance and, in some products, added height.

name: Gynecomastia compression vest
summary: A tight vest that hides male chest tissue under clothes; it conceals gynecomastia but no studies test it.
lead: A gynecomastia compression vest is a tight-fitting undershirt or vest, sold mainly to men, that presses the chest flat so that enlarged male breast tissue is less visible under clothing. It conceals rather than treats the condition. Gynecomastia is the benign enlargement of one or both male breasts caused by an imbalance between estrogens and androgens.

name: Spray-tan booth
summary: Automated booth that mists DHA for a UV-free tan; the colour is reliable, but inhalation safety is unstudied in humans.
lead: A spray-tan booth is an enclosed, automated cabin in which a fine mist of a sunless tanning solution is sprayed over the body. The active ingredient is dihydroxyacetone (DHA), a colourless sugar that reacts with amino acids in the dead outer layer of skin to produce a temporary brown colour. Professionals can also apply the solution by hand with an airbrush.

name: Bronzer
summary: A wash-off skin tint that gives an instant tanned look with no UV and no staying power.
lead: A bronzer is a cosmetic product that temporarily tints the skin to look tanned. It comes as powders, lotions, gels, mousses, sprays and tinted moisturizers, and the colour lasts until it is washed off with soap and water. It is often worn for a one-day tan or alongside a longer-lasting self-tanner.
claims: Bronzer on the face avoids the 'ghost face' left by a body-only tan
Bronzer is a safer substitute for sun exposure on the face
Bodybuilders need a spray tan plus bronzer on stage because a real tan is not dark enough

name: Gradual tanning lotion
summary: A daily moisturizer with a mild self-tanning agent that builds a streak-resistant colour over several days.
lead: A gradual tanning lotion, also called a build-up tanner, is a lotion or moisturizer that contains a mild self-tanning agent so that colour deepens with repeated daily use. Encyclopedic sources say a slight change in skin colour is usually visible after the first application and darkens with more frequent use.

name: Tanning accelerator
summary: Topical or oral products, often tyrosine or psoralen-based, sold to speed up a UV tan; efficacy is unproven and users report more acne and rashes.
lead: Tanning accelerators are topical products, and sometimes pills, sold to speed up or deepen tanning when combined with UV exposure from sunlight or tanning beds. The ingredients described in the literature include tyrosine, psoralens and other chemicals. Wikipedia describes them as lotions or pills, usually containing tyrosine, that claim to boost melanin formation, and states that no scientific data currently supports these claims.

name: UPF clothing
summary: Fabric tested and labelled for how much UV it blocks, used as a no-reapplication alternative to sunscreen.
lead: UPF clothing, also called sun-protective clothing, is apparel made from fabrics rated for ultraviolet protection. The ultraviolet protection factor (UPF) is the ratio of sunburn-causing UV that passes through a fabric without it versus with it, similar in concept to sunscreen's SPF but measured with laboratory instruments rather than human sunburn testing.

name: Light box / SAD lamp
summary: A bright-light lamp used for seasonal depression, with solid evidence for SAD and none yet for looks.
lead: A light box, commonly called a SAD lamp, is a device that gives off bright white light, typically up to 10,000 lux at a set distance, used for bright light therapy (BLT). It is the standard form of light therapy for seasonal affective disorder (SAD), a condition of recurrent winter depression that affects about 1 to 3 percent of adults in temperate climates and is more common in women.
claims: Consumer SAD lamps are too weak to work unless held very close
A light lamp can fix winter tiredness and low mood

name: Mattress (medium-firm)
summary: A middle-firmness mattress that sleep research links to less back pain, and that forums link to posture; nothing tests facial or skeletal looks.
lead: A medium-firm mattress is a bed with an intermediate firmness rating, between soft and firm. Mattresses come in innerspring, foam (polyurethane, memory foam, latex), hybrid, air and water types, and no single numeric firmness scale is given in encyclopedic sources. A 2003 trial used the European Committee for Standardization's Hs scale.
claims: A soft mattress that sags under the lower back causes back pain
Medium-firm is the right firmness
Sleeping on the floor or a very flat, hard surface is better

name: Home UVB booth
summary: A stand-up narrowband UVB phototherapy cabinet meant for home skin treatment; it is a medical light device, and its use for cosmetic tanning has not been studied.
lead: A home UVB booth is a stand-up cabinet fitted with narrowband ultraviolet-B (NB-UVB) lamps, designed so that a person can receive whole-body phototherapy at home instead of attending a clinic. Narrowband UVB emits around 311-313 nanometres and is the most widely used form of phototherapy in dermatology . A large, high-power UVB booth can deliver full-body treatment at home as an alternative to office-based treatment .
claims: Booths with a low UVB percentage give the deepest tan with the least burning.
A 'base tan' from a booth is a myth that offers little protection against burning outdoors.

name: Concealer (for men)
summary: A pigmented cosmetic dabbed over dark circles, blemishes and redness to even out skin tone; a temporary cover rather than a treatment, with little male-specific research.
lead: Concealer is a cosmetic used to mask skin imperfections such as dark under-eye circles, blemishes and hyperpigmentation. It is similar to foundation but more heavily pigmented, usually applied in small amounts and then blended with a brush, sponge or fingertips . It can be worn over or under foundation, or on its own .
claims: Concealer is one of the most effective cheap 'looksmaxes', especially for people with permanent dark eye bags.
Concealer can be applied so that it does not look like makeup.
Men wearing concealer face social stigma and conceal their use.

name: Eyebrow pencil / powder
summary: Pencils and powders that fill sparse or uneven brows with pigment; a daily-wear cosmetic with essentially no published research behind it.
lead: Eyebrow pencils and powders are cosmetics used to define the eyebrows or make them appear fuller, outlining the shape or filling sparse areas . Brow gels add texture so hairs look thicker, and brow powders or eyeshadows closely matched to natural hair colour suit people who want a softer, fuller look . Pencils in general, including concealer pencils, can also be used to define eyebrows .

name: Hair styling clay & pomade
summary: Wax-, oil- or clay-based products that hold and texture hair for a day; styling aids with no clinical research behind them.
lead: Hair clay and pomade are styling products used to shape and hold hair. Pomade is a greasy, waxy or water-based product that gives a shiny, slick appearance, holds longer than most hair products and often takes repeated washes to remove . Clay is a related category of styling product; general encyclopedic coverage of it is thin .

name: Cologne / perfume
summary: Alcohol-based fragrance worn for scent and impression; popular in grooming circles, with no published trials of its effect on attractiveness in the sources reviewed.
lead: Perfume is a mixture of fragrant essential oils or aroma compounds, fixatives and solvents, usually in liquid form. Fine fragrance typically uses ethanol or an ethanol-water mix as the solvent . Products are classed by concentration, from parfum or extrait at about 15-30% down through eau de parfum, eau de toilette and eau de cologne at about 2-3%, though the terms are imprecise and brands differ .
claims: Cologne only works if you are already good-looking.

name: Rhinoplasty
summary: Surgery that reshapes the nose for looks or breathing; the most discussed facial 'harmony' operation in looksmaxxing, with real revision and complication rates.
lead: Rhinoplasty, informally a 'nose job', is plastic surgery that changes the shape, size or proportions of the nose or improves its function. It takes two broad forms: reconstructive surgery, which restores form and function after injury, birth defects or failed earlier surgery, and cosmetic surgery, which changes appearance . Surgery limited to the septum is called septoplasty .
claims: The nose drives midface harmony, so reshaping it changes the whole face.
Fillers only camouflage, while surgery permanently reshapes bone and cartilage.
Rhinoplasty can go wrong and make a face look worse or 'fake'.
Rhinoplasty is 'cope' for men.

name: Bimaxillary osteotomy (bimax)
summary: Double-jaw surgery that repositions both upper and lower jaw; an established operation for bite and airway problems that forums also treat as the big facial-structure move.
lead: Bimaxillary osteotomy, commonly called bimax or double-jaw surgery, is a form of orthognathic (corrective jaw) surgery in which both the upper jaw and the lower jaw are cut, repositioned and fixed in a new position, usually through incisions inside the mouth. It is used for bite discrepancies, jaw-joint problems, facial asymmetry and obstructive sleep apnoea, and is also sought by people who want to change facial proportions.
claims: Bimax can be covered by insurance if there is a functional bite problem such as an underbite.
Braces are needed before and after bimax, and stay on during the operation.
Bimax with counter-clockwise rotation gives a better-looking profile than the same patient's current appearance suggests.
Bimax improves overall facial harmony and the airway at the same time.

name: LeFort 1 maxillary advancement
summary: Upper-jaw surgery that cuts and moves the maxilla forward for midface projection; a standard orthognathic operation whose cosmetic claims rest mostly on bite and cleft research.
lead: Le Fort I osteotomy is an upper-jaw operation in which the maxilla is cut horizontally above the roots of the teeth, mobilised and fixed in a new position, usually through an incision inside the mouth. It is the most common maxillary procedure in orthognathic surgery and can advance, set back, shorten, lengthen or expand the upper jaw. In looksmaxxing circles it is known as LeFort 1 or maxilla advancement and is discussed as a method of increasing midface projection.
claims: Advancing the upper jaw also improves under-eye support and the infraorbital area.
Maxilla advancement of roughly 4 to 10 mm is the usual goal.
Le Fort I with a lower-jaw operation can be covered by insurance for an underbite.
Surgical movements are stable once healed.

name: Maxillomandibular advancement (MMA)
summary: Surgery that moves both jaws forward, established as a sleep-apnoea operation and marketed online as a looks-plus-airway upgrade.
lead: Maxillomandibular advancement (MMA), also called bimaxillary advancement or Bi-Max, is a jaw operation that moves both the upper jaw and the lower jaw forward. It originated in orthognathic surgery for facial skeletal deformity and bite problems and was later applied to obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), where it is classed as a type of sleep surgery.
claims: MMA after skeletal expansion could cause the cheeks to drop and lose expansion gains.
Moving both jaws forward gives a looks improvement together with an airway benefit.

name: Jaw surgery (orthognathic)
summary: Corrective jaw surgery that repositions the upper jaw, lower jaw and chin for bite, airway and facial-balance goals; a legitimate surgical field that forums treat as the big structural lever.
lead: Orthognathic surgery, also called corrective jaw surgery, reshapes the jaws and lower face to treat structural, growth, airway, jaw-joint and bite problems, and can also be used for facial balance and symmetry. The operation is usually done through the mouth: bone is cut, moved and fixed in a new position, and it is typically coordinated with orthodontic treatment.
claims: Bimax or a single-jaw operation can fix a recessed jaw, and the result is often better than a jaw-jut test suggests.
Jaw surgery carries serious risks that are underreported, including permanent numbness.
Jaw surgery can improve function but disappoint cosmetically.
Getting insurance to cover jaw surgery depends on proving a functional problem.

name: Chin implant / genioplasty
summary: Two ways to build out the chin, a placed implant or a cut-and-slid piece of the jawbone; routine cosmetic and orthognathic surgery with the larger changes coming from bone.
lead: Chin augmentation, also called mentoplasty or genioplasty, changes the underlying structure of the chin to balance the rest of the face; it can add projection with an implant, reduce or round the chin through bone cutting, or change its height. Sliding genioplasty uses an osteotomy of the chin bone, while implants are placed in a pocket over the bone, usually through an incision inside the mouth or under the chin.
claims: Sliding genioplasty gives a bigger, more reliable change than a chin implant.
A few millimetres of advancement is enough for an average chin.
A chin procedure alone may not solve a profile problem caused by the jaws.

name: Jaw implants
summary: Implants placed along the angle and body of the lower jaw to widen or define it; used in facial gender surgery and cosmetic work, with little outcome research behind the forum hype.
lead: Jaw implants are alloplastic (manufactured) implants placed over the angle and body of the mandible to increase width and definition; they are also called mandibular angle or gonial angle implants. A review of lower jaw contouring in facial gender-affirming surgery describes augmentation of the mandibular angle, body and chin with alloplastic implants, fat or bone as a masculinising option and reports that complications are minimal, while stating that more research on outcomes is needed.
claims: Being a little overweight at the time of surgery does not change the final implant result once weight is lost.
Jaw implants look bloated or unnatural on people with a short or recessed mandible.

name: Cheek implants
summary: Solid silicone or polyethylene implants over the cheekbone for more projection; reviews report high satisfaction but a few percent to ~10% complication rates, and little trial-grade evidence.
lead: Cheek implants, also called malar or submalar implants, are solid alloplastic (synthetic) devices placed over or beneath the cheekbone to increase midface projection or fullness. They are used to correct congenital cheekbone underdevelopment, asymmetry and age-related volume loss, and in gender-affirming facial surgery, and they are discussed in looksmaxxing communities as a way to obtain higher or more angular cheekbones.
claims: Most cheek implants are the 'apple cheek' submalar type, which gives a bloated look, while malar implants give a defined, angular look.
Custom-designed implants are better than off-the-shelf implants.
Cheek implants can approximate the effect of a Le Fort III midface advancement.
Implants are a safe and permanent option when done by a skilled surgeon.

name: Buccal fat removal
summary: Intraoral removal of the cheek's buccal fat pad for a slimmer, hollower look; permanent, with a 25% pooled postoperative complication rate and no randomised trials.
lead: Buccal fat removal, also called bichectomy or buccal fat pad extraction, is a cosmetic operation that takes out part of the buccal fat pad (Bichat's fat pad), a deep encapsulated pad of fat in each cheek, to slim the lower midface and create a more contoured or hollow-cheeked look. It is usually done through a small incision inside the mouth.
claims: Buccal fat removal gives leaner, more sculpted cheeks that dieting cannot.
Removal can leave a person looking gaunt or worse than before.
The operation is low-risk and minor.
Fat grafting can restore volume if removal goes too far.

name: Lateral canthoplasty
summary: Surgery on the outer eye corner, used medically for lid laxity and increasingly sought to raise canthal tilt; no studies test it for that cosmetic aim.
lead: Lateral canthoplasty is eyelid surgery that repositions or tightens the lateral canthus, the outer corner of the eye where the upper and lower lids meet. In ophthalmic and plastic surgery it is used mainly to support or tighten a lax lower eyelid, to prevent or correct lid malposition after lower blepharoplasty, and in facial palsy and ectropion repair.
claims: Canthoplasty can raise the outer eye corner for a more positive canthal tilt.
Canthopexy is the better choice than canthoplasty for people under 40.
Canthoplasty carries a meaningful risk of botching the eye.
Canthoplasty can be done at home.

name: Hunter eyes surgery
summary: Slang for combined eye-corner surgery (canthopexy, fat grafts, blepharoplasty) aimed at a deep-set, positively tilted look; no study tests that goal.
lead: 'Hunter eyes' is looksmaxxing slang for an eye appearance usually described as deep-set, with little upper eyelid show, a low brow-to-lid distance, and a neutral or positive canthal tilt. 'Hunter eyes surgery' is the community term for surgical combinations intended to produce that look, most often canthopexy or canthoplasty at the outer eye corner, sometimes combined with fat grafting, brow or blepharoplasty procedures.
claims: Canthopexy can create hunter eyes or a more positive canthal tilt.
Combined surgeries, including fat grafting, produce a more hunter look than any one procedure.
Canthopexy adds millimetres of palpebral fissure length.

name: Orbital decompression
summary: Orbital bone or fat removal that lets the eye sit deeper; a thyroid-eye-disease operation with no trials for cosmetic deep-setting.
lead: Orbital decompression is surgery that enlarges the effective volume of the eye socket by removing orbital bone, orbital fat, or both, allowing the eye to sit further back. Its established use is in thyroid eye disease (Graves' orbitopathy), where swollen muscle and fat push the eye forward (proptosis) and can compress the optic nerve.
claims: Orbital decompression is the way to get deep-set eyes if yours protrude.
Only people with genuinely bulging eyes are candidates; others should use fat grafts instead.
The surgery is high-risk and can cause botched or sight-threatening outcomes.
Surgeons differ on whether to remove fat or bone, and this changes results.

name: Blepharoplasty
summary: Eyelid surgery to remove or reposition excess skin and fat; established for hooding and bags, with no trials for looksmaxxing-specific eye-shape goals.
lead: Blepharoplasty, commonly called eyelid surgery, is plastic surgery that removes or repositions excess skin, muscle and fat of the upper or lower eyelids. It is performed for functional reasons, such as heavy upper lids that reduce peripheral vision, and for cosmetic reasons, such as reducing hooding or under-eye bags.
claims: Blepharoplasty with fat grafting can 'ascend' the eye area.
Eyelid surgery can fix a droopy or ptotic eye and its apparent asymmetry.
Blepharoplasty reliably removes tired-looking bags and hooding.
